source.title: Diversified Scaling Inference in Time Series Foundation Models
source.authors: Rui-Jin Hua; Zichuan Liu; Kun Zhang; Yiyuan Yang

record.file_problem: none; the full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: Tests downstream forecasting performance against model scale in time-series foundation models, a different setting from language-model pretraining scaling.
record.gate_note: The study measures inference-time forecasting MSE, not held-out language-model pretraining cross-entropy, training tokens, training compute, or a compute-optimal parameter/token allocation. Its results on model size and downstream forecasting performance bear on V6. Inference-sampling and perturbation results are related but do not test the listed training-scaling versions.
record.test_reason: The study compares forecasting MSE across released sizes of time-series foundation models (Chronos-T5 8M–710M, Moirai 55M–1.24B, TimeMoE 50M/200M). It frames this explicitly against Kaplan-style parameter scaling. This is a time-series (non-text) setting, so the model-size results bear on V5, not V6, which concerns downstream tasks of language models. The evidence is weak as a scaling test: it uses off-the-shelf checkpoints, few sizes, no power-law fit, and MSE taken after best-of-N or median aggregation.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct. The authors find that model size and context length give inconsistent, dataset-dependent gains under standard sampling, which saturates. Diversified input perturbations with validated strategies improve forecasting by up to ~50% under larger inference budgets. They propose RobustMSE as a budget-fixed evaluation metric.
record.recipe_differences: Inference-only forecasting evaluation of time-series foundation models; measures MSE under model-size and inference-budget changes rather than language-model pretraining cross-entropy against parameter, token, or training-compute scaling laws.
record.method_sensitivity: Outcomes vary with dataset, model family and size, context length, temperature, aggregation method, perturbation type, and perturbation relevance/fidelity.

fits_no_version.finding: Standard repeated sampling improves MSE but saturates; temperature effects depend on sampling budget and decoding capability.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Inference-time sample scaling in TSFMs saturates under a fixed predictive distribution.

fits_no_version.finding: Input-perturbed diversified sampling lowers MSE with sample budget, by up to ~50% versus a single standard sample; gains depend on perturbation and model.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Input diversification extends inference-time scaling gains in TSFMs when perturbations preserve fidelity.

record.code_released: The paper says code is available in Diversified-ScalingInference-in-TSFMs; URL not stated.
record.peer_reviewed: preprint; venue listed as arXiv.org, and the paper states “Under Review.”
record.problems: The results concern inference-time forecasting rather than language-model training losses. The text describes many scaling curves without tabulated numerical values; several plotted results are figure-only. The reported trends are explicitly dataset- and model-dependent.
record.rows_left_out: Not applicable; five relevant rows retained. The paper contains many additional per-dataset and per-perturbation inference results, but they do not measure the listed training-loss scaling versions; representative aggregate inference findings are recorded in R4 and R5.

untested.parts: No pretraining-loss sweep over parameters, tokens or compute for language models.
No fits on small runs extrapolated to larger runs.
No shape comparison at fixed parameter count.
Power-law form itself (no fit), and scaling in data or compute rather than parameters.
No exponent fitting or comparison of fitting choices.

missing.what: Chronos-T5 model-size MSE values on ETTh1 (EM and MV, no perturbation): non-monotonic, minimum at Small (46M).
TimeMoE 50M vs 200M across context lengths: 200M is no better and is sometimes worse (e.g. Traffic L=512: 0.3205 vs 0.3260).
Chronos model-size curves on Electricity and Traffic, described as irregular, with the optimal size shifting by dataset.

record.verdict_notes: The model-size evidence is weak as a scaling-law test. It compares released checkpoints with few sizes per family and fits no power law. MSE is measured after EM (oracle best-of-N) or MV aggregation over 128 samples. Evaluation sets overlap pretraining for TimesFM (Electricity, Traffic). The reader's V6 link was wrong because V6 concerns language-model downstream tasks; the non-text setting fits V5.

versions.untested_parts: No held-out pretraining loss sweep over parameters, tokens, or training compute.
No small-run fits or forecasts of much larger training runs.
No fixed training-compute budget or parameter/token allocation analysis.
No controlled comparison of depth, width, or architecture at fixed parameter count.
Time-series forecasting is evaluated, but the study does not test whether pretraining-loss power laws transfer to other modalities or training regimes.
Tests model-size trends in time-series forecasting, but not performance as a function of language-model pretraining loss or on other downstream task families.
Does not fit or compare training-loss exponents, compute-optimal splits, or alternative training-loss fitting choices.
